analysis.title: Enter The Dragon: Hartnett Says China Is Now The Biggest Risk To Global Earnings, Here's Why
key_insights: Hartnett's Flow Show 'Enter the Dragon' names China exporting deflation as the biggest risk to global earnings. China high-tech exports hit a record $147B in September, up 63% YoY, and total exports are up 36% YoY, despite a yuan at a 4-year high.

The CSI 300 is down 20% since June and in a bear market, with the CSI 300 Information Technology index down 41%. It posted its 10th straight weekly decline, the most oversold in LSEG's history. China 10Y yields are at a record low 1.6%, a deflation combination of falling stocks and yields with a rising currency.

Consensus 2026 earnings growth for MSCI China has fallen from more than 11% at the start of the year to barely 1%, per BofA. Southbound flows flipped to net selling. Property investment is still down 20% YoY.
Goldman estimates Chinese households hold about RMB 63 trillion in excess deposits with a savings rate of 33.4%, so liquidity is ample but spending is weak.

EPFR shows a $17.0B inflow to China equities this week, the largest since July. The article attributes it to Beijing support (buybacks, liquidity injections, limits on institutional selling), and BofA argues national-team buying is more likely to set a floor than start a sustainable rally.

Meta's 'capex wall' triggered an AI funding scare. The Nasdaq 100 had its worst day since June (-2.9%), the SOX fell more than 6%, and hedge funds had their worst session since 2011. Treasuries had their best day in over a year, taking the 10Y to 4.97%, the first close below 5% in a month.

Goldman rates strategists price just 2.1bps of hikes for the Oct 28 FOMC after the Fed passed on a hike despite hot CPI. BofA's US economists still expect 25bps, but call it a 'heavy lift' given the week's price action.

Hartnett reads the October selloff as a tech de-rating in a tightening cycle, not a macro problem. Mid caps (MDY >137), small caps (IJR >125) and global financials (IXG >666) are holding, NDX holds 28k, and Berkshire hit records. Tech growth 'tells' to watch are MAGS <70, TSM <400, and EPS downward revisions.

Hartnett stays tactically risk-off until mid-November. He expects yields down (GT30 toward 5%), stocks down and the dollar down (DXY below 100) until three things happen: a midterm Democratic sweep is fully priced, the ECB/French government stop the rout in French bonds, and an AI capex cut or extreme equity issuance peaks hyperscaler debt spreads.

Meta's Schedule 14C filing for new non-voting Class C shares says it expects 'to raise hundreds of billions of dollars over a period of several years beginning as early as fall 2026'. The article calls this a possible 'Boeing 2024 moment'. Hartnett's AI hyperscaler 10Y-30Y spread index is at 130bps, up from 60 in about a year. His downside trigger is 200bps.
Polymarket puts a Democratic sweep at 68%, and Trump's approval is 33% on the economy and 27% on inflation. Hartnett has warned a sweep would mean a 10%+ 'skid' for stocks.

The 10Y OAT-Bund spread hit 178bps intraday Thursday, the widest since the EU debt crisis. Hartnett's line in the sand is 180bps, against the Nov 2011 peak of 189bps. Moody's took no action on France Friday night.

Hartnett's contrarian view is to add bonds and 'peak yield' plays (small cap, REITs, utilities, consumer discretionary), under the rule 'sell hubris, buy humiliation'. The 10-year rolling return on US Treasuries is -1%, below the Dec 1959 and Sep 1981 lows, and long-run Treasury returns are the worst in 100 years.

Goldman's Delta One desk and Codacci-Pisanelli say a growth scare helps duration but a recession would bring heavy Treasury supply, and the rally 'does not fully solve the imbalance' between Treasury supply and demand. Brent is above $117 while bonds rally, a divergence The Market Ear summed up as 'oil screams inflation, bonds scream recession'.

Weekly flows through Wednesday: $55.6B to stocks, $28.8B to cash, $12.1B to bonds, $2.6B to gold, $0.2B to crypto. Tech had a $18.8B inflow (largest since Jul'26), one day before the Nasdaq's worst session since June. Consumer funds had a $2.1B outflow (largest since Feb'14) and utilities a $1.6B outflow (largest since Mar'15).

The BofA Bull & Bear Indicator fell to 7.2 from 7.4, so the sell signal that began May 26 has ended. FMS positioning remains at the 100th percentile and breadth is the only bearish component (27th percentile). The Breadth Rule shows a net 30% of global indices oversold versus the 88% needed for a contrarian buy signal.

Hartnett's three 2027 scenarios are bubble, breadth and bust. The AI Big 10 is 41% of the market, the level at which the Nifty Fifty, Japan and TMT bubbles peaked (railroads peaked at 63%). Consensus expects global tech EPS +43% in 2027 after +92% in 2026, and 4.7% US nominal GDP growth. 'No AI boom = no boom.'
Gold fell below $4,000, its lowest in more than three months, and is -6.9% YTD, just 0.2 points ahead of bitcoin at -7.1%. Oil is +72.7% YTD, US stocks +11.9%, global stocks +8.7%.

The author (Zero Hedge) adds an opinion that the 6% of fund managers expecting a hard landing looks 'absurdly cheap' and that this week's action resembles early stages of a bust. This is the author's view, not Hartnett's.

French bond rout: OAT-Bund spread breaking 180bps (Nov 2011 peak 189bps) and a Moody's downgrade risk.
AI capex cut or extreme equity issuance (Meta's planned raise of hundreds of billions).
China exporting deflation and 2027 earnings forecasts (global tech EPS +43%) that only work if the AI boom continues.
Recession, which would bring Treasury supply and deficit risk and end the bond rally.

vol_and_positioning: Hedge funds had their worst session since 2011 on Thursday after the Meta-driven AI selloff.

BofA FMS positioning is at the 100th percentile and fund managers have barely sold. Investors are the most overweight tech since Aug'20, and 50% predict 'no landing', 40% 'soft landing' and 6% 'hard landing' in the Oct FMS.
The Bull & Bear Indicator fell to 7.2. Breadth is at the 27th percentile, and bearish hedge fund positioning in oil and S&P 500 futures is a contributing factor.

The Breadth Rule shows a net 30% of global equity indices oversold (from 52% last week) versus 88% needed for a buy signal. It would take US, Taiwan and Brazil indices falling another 5-10% to get there.
Consumer fund outflows ($2.1B) and utility fund outflows ($1.6B) were each the 2nd largest on record, which Hartnett reads as capitulation.
Hyperscaler spread trigger: the 10Y-30Y spread index is at 130bps and a surge above 200bps would signal deleveraging on shadow banking credit event risk.
geopolitical: Gulf escalation, with Houthi strikes on Saudi Arabia pushing Brent above $117 (highest since May) and reports of post-midterm US/Israeli strikes on Iran.
French debt scare, with the OAT-Bund spread at 178bps, Moody's taking no action, and far-left riots with 70,000 police deployed for a second weekend.
A Trump peace plan outline for Ukraine was circulating Friday. Hartnett's upside risk is Russia/Ukraine/Iran peace deals cutting oil $10-20/bbl.
US midterms Nov 3, with Polymarket at 68% Democratic sweep and 28% Democratic House/GOP Senate.
US-China AI competition and tariffs. Hartnett sees a Democratic sweep reducing Trump's ability to coerce resources and capital into the US-China AI priority.
Brazil election Oct 25 (Polymarket 78% Bolsonaro, 22% Lula) and Israel election Oct 27 (48% Eizenkot, 28% Netanyahu).
APEC summit in Shenzhen Nov 18, with Xi, Trump and Putin all attending.
